properties.name: camel.component.iggy.auto-commit
properties.description: Whether the server stores the offset of the consumer group when it returns the polled messages, before the route processes them. If false, the consumer polls from startingOffset and keeps the offset in memory only, so it starts again from startingOffset after a restart.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.auto-create-stream
properties.description: Whether to create the stream if it does not exist. The producer and the consumer check it when they start, and the producer again for each message that has an override header.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.auto-create-topic
properties.description: Whether to create the topic if it does not exist, with the partitionsCount, compressionAlgorithm, messageExpiry, maxTopicSize and iggyHeaderOptions options. The producer and the consumer check it when they start, and the producer again for each message that has an override header.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.bridge-error-handler
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.client-transport
properties.description: The transport that the client uses to connect to the Iggy server.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.compression-algorithm
properties.description: The compression algorithm of a topic that autoCreateTopic creates.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.configuration
properties.description: Allows to pre-configure the Iggy component with common options that the endpoints will reuse. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.iggy.IggyConfiguration type.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.consumer-group-name
properties.description: The name of the consumer group that the consumer joins, and creates if it does not exist. Required for the consumer.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.consumers-count
properties.description: The number of threads of the thread pool of the consumer. The consumer runs one polling task, so one thread polls the topic.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the iggy component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.host
properties.description: The hostname or IP address of the Iggy server.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.iggy-header-options
properties.description: Additional options of a topic that autoCreateTopic creates, as key-value pairs that are sent to the server as strings, for example durability.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.max-topic-size
properties.description: The maximum size in bytes of a topic that autoCreateTopic creates. With 0 no maximum size is set on the topic.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.message-expiry
properties.description: The time in seconds after which the server deletes the messages of a topic that autoCreateTopic creates. With 0 no expiry is set on the topic.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.partition-id
properties.description: The ID of the partition that the consumer polls. If not set, the server chooses the partition for the member of the consumer group.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.partitioning
properties.description: How the producer chooses the partition of the messages it sends, as an org.apache.iggy.message.Partitioning: balanced() spreads them over the partitions, partitionId(Long) sends to one partition and messagesKey(String) to the partition of a key. The option is a org.apache.iggy.message.Partitioning type.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.partitions-count
properties.description: The number of partitions of a topic that autoCreateTopic creates.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.password
properties.description: The password that the client logs in with to the Iggy server. Required, together with the username option: the client fails to connect without them.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.poll-batch-size
properties.description: The maximum number of messages that the consumer polls in one request.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.polling-strategy
properties.description: Where the consumer polls from when autoCommit is true: next polls the messages after the offset stored for the consumer group, first the first messages of the partition, and last the last messages of the partition.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.port
properties.description: The port of the Iggy server. The default 8090 is the default port of the TCP transport of the server, so set the HTTP port of the server when clientTransport is HTTP.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.shutdown-timeout
properties.description: The time in milliseconds that the consumer waits for its polling thread to finish when it stops, before it interrupts the thread.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.ssl-context-parameters
properties.description: SSL configuration using an org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters instance. This takes precedence over tlsEnabled and tlsCertificatePath when configured. The option is a org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters type.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.starting-offset
properties.description: The offset of the first message that the consumer polls when autoCommit is false. 0 is the first message of the partition.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.stream-id
properties.description: The ID of a stream that autoCreateStream looks up: if no stream has this ID, a stream named streamName is created. The producer and the consumer always address the stream by its name.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.stream-name
properties.description: The name of the stream that holds the topic. Required. The CamelIggyStreamOverride header replaces it for the producer.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.tls-certificate-path
properties.description: The path to a certificate file in PEM format that the client trusts for the TLS connection to the Iggy server. If not set, the client uses the default trust store of the JVM.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.tls-enabled
properties.description: Whether the client connects to the Iggy server over TLS.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.use-global-ssl-context-parameters
properties.description: Enable usage of global SSL context parameters.

properties.name: camel.component.iggy.username
properties.description: The username that the client logs in with to the Iggy server. Required, together with the password option: the client fails to connect without them.
